provenance: found by running live-hn-item1-submitter (report 20260817-024235, M6 eval-first batch). The case was written with the contract-advertised `near:` key; the resolver has never implemented it, and the freeze note said so. What the run exposed is worse than the drift: the unresolvable key is DROPPED SILENTLY. `{role: link, near: ...}` resolved as a bare `{role: link}` -> 39 matches -> ResolveError, so the run failed for ambiguity and never said that half its plan's meaning had evaporated. This case uses a key that is not in the schema at all (`nearest`), so it stays red-worthy after `near:` lands.

triage.what_this_grades: not whether a key is implemented — whether an unimplemented one is LOUD. Plan semantics the executor cannot honour must stop the run as failure:task, the class specs/001 reserves for a plan the executor cannot honour. Degrading to a weaker target is the same family of defect as answering from a page the agent never reached: the run reports a result for a task it silently changed.
triage.watched_red: today: failure:locate (ambiguous-match on the degraded target). Wanted: failure:task naming the unknown key.
